title: Quantum LDPC codes with design rate 1/5 and good performance below 1000 physical qubits
abstract: Constant-rate quantum low-density parity-check (LDPC) codes promise fault-tolerant quantum computation with constant spatial overhead in the asymptotic limit. Nonetheless, discovering finite-length code instances with good practical performance remains challenging. We introduce a new family of quantum LDPC codes with design rate $1/5$ and check weight $9$ that approaches the teraquop memory regime per qubit-round with several hundred physical qubits, under idling-free circuit-level noise of strength $0.1\%$ and GPU-accelerated Relay-belief-propagation (Relay-BP) decoding with average latencies around 1-2 ms, a regime relevant to trapped-ion and neutral-atom processors. The construction involves the balanced product of classical LDPC codes with design rate $1/2$ that share non-abelian $\mathbb{Z}_\ell \rtimes \mathbb{Z}_m$ group symmetries, which may be of independent interest for classical error correction. We build syndrome extraction circuits tailored to reconfigurable atom arrays using a simple greedy scheduler, with single-round rearrangement times around 30-60 ms using present hardware specifications, and substantial room for future improvements. We also construct logical Pauli bases that are equivariant with respect to the group symmetry, which can significantly compress the design space for code surgery. Together, these results further advance the practicality of constant-rate quantum LDPC codes for near-term, fault-tolerant quantum computers.
summary: This paper presents a novel family of quantum LDPC codes designed to improve fault tolerance in near-term quantum computers. By leveraging group symmetries, they achieve high code rates (1/5) while keeping the physical qubit count manageable ($\lesssim 1000$). The work validates these codes through detailed circuit simulations and benchmarking against state-of-the-art decoding hardware.
main_problem: The challenge is discovering finite-length quantum Low-Density Parity-Check (qLDPC) code instances that exhibit good practical performance for fault-tolerant quantum computation.
main_result: The authors introduce a new family of qLDPC codes with design rate 1/5, demonstrating high encoding efficiency and achieving low logical error rates in the near-term regime using physical qubits below 1000.
method: The construction involves building these codes via the balanced product of classical LDPC codes sharing non-abelian group symmetries, followed by detailed circuit simulation and GPU benchmarking for decoding.
model_or_system: The work is tailored for near-term quantum processors like trapped ions and neutral atoms, focusing on physical implementations involving syndrome extraction circuits scheduled for reconfigurable atom arrays.
key_observables: Logical error rate (LER) per qubit-round, circuit distance ($d_{circ}$), decoding latencies (1-2 ms), and memory efficiency ratios ($	ext{k}d^2/n$).
important_parameters: Design rate of 1/5; physical size below 1000 qubits; idling-free noise strength of $0.1\%$.
main_assumptions: The practical performance relies on assumptions regarding hardware compatibility, the specific noise model used, and the potential suboptimality of the Relay-BP decoder at low noise.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate memory efficiency vs. size and LER vs. noise strength; tables detail code parameters (Table 1) and gate schedules/latencies across different GPUs (Tables 14, 16).
paper_structure: The paper progresses from establishing the need for high-rate qLDPC codes to detailing the ZSZ group construction methods, proving structural limitations like unavoidable 4-cycles in symmetric products, and finally validating performance through circuit simulations and decoding benchmarks.
why_interesting: It directly addresses hardware constraints by providing concrete, implementable code structures (ZSZ-LP) optimized for specific physical platforms (trapped ions/neutral atoms), bridging the gap between theoretical bounds and near-term device capabilities.
